Matching literature supports explicit overlap checks, prespecified calipers, and balance assessment before interpreting perturbation effects. Austin’s simulations recommend a caliper of 0.2 SD of the logit propensity score for particular treatment-effect settings; this is not a universal threshold for text similarity or transition probabilities ([Austin, 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20925139/)). A practical adaptation: match within dataset on training-history length, item log-popularity, transition support, and title/description similarity, excluding the feature deliberately perturbed. For sparse transitions, use a documented smoothed estimate, e.g. P(j|i)=[n(i,j)+αP(j)]/[n(i)+α], while retaining raw counts as reliability indicators. This formula is a proposed diagnostic design, not an established result from the matching papers. Report unmatched fractions, match distances, reuse counts, and standardized covariate differences; restrict conclusions to supported histories rather than forcing distant matches.

Repeated perturbations of one user do not create independent users. For the 20-user panel, first average paired score/rank changes within user, then macro-average across categories. Report individual-user effects and leave-one-user-out sensitivity alongside uncertainty. Cluster-robust methods address within-user dependence, but few clusters can make conventional intervals unreliable; a small-sample correction or wild cluster bootstrap merits consideration ([Cameron–Miller](https://faculty.econ.ucdavis.edu/faculty/cameron/research/Cameron_Miller_JHR_2014_July_09.pdf)). Distinguish uncertainty conditional on fixed matches from uncertainty that includes matching. Naively bootstrapping and rematching fixed-neighbor estimators can fail ([Abadie–Imbens](https://economics.mit.edu/sites/default/files/publications/ON%20THE%20FAILURE%20OF%20THE%20BOOTSTRAP%20FOR.pdf)). These diagnostics measure model sensitivity under observed matching constraints; they cannot identify unobserved user conformity or diversity traits.
